articles.title: Trump Media group stares down $1bn debt crunch as bitcoin bet fades
articles.summary: The Trump family's media group may soon be forced to sell hundreds of millions' worth of assets, including some of its crypto holdings, or take...
articles.body:
The Trump family's media group may soon be forced to sell hundreds of millions' worth of assets, including some of its crypto holdings, or take on costly new borrowing as it comes under pressure to repay up to $1bn in debt.

Trump Media & Technology Group (TMTG), which runs the Truth Social app and is controlled by Donald Trump's family, faces a November 30 deadline to repay convertible bonds it sold last May to fund its creation of a "bitcoin treasury" to hoard digital currency.

But shares in TMTG have plunged and bitcoin has fallen by about a third in the past year, despite the Trump administration ushering in a more permissive era for cryptocurrencies.

The company's waning share price, which is down more than 60 per cent this year to $4.64, has meant lenders to the company who had hoped to convert their notes to stock at $34.72 are deeply out of the money.

Noteholders have therefore been left with little incentive to hold the bonds rather than forcing the company to repay them for cash at face value at the end of the month.

The Trump family media group has placed crypto at the heart of its business, with its former chief executive and chair Devin Nunes calling it a "crucial part of our assets".

Despite President Trump previously calling bitcoin a "scam" in 2021, he has become an ardent supporter of the asset in his second term and pledged to make the US the "crypto capital of the world".

A potential debt redemption of $1bn would further strain the lossmaking media group's finances and could force it to part with some of its cryptocurrency investments, the company's most valuable asset worth around $1.36bn at the end of the third quarter.

TMTG reported a loss of $234mn for the nine months to September.

One investor who is demanding repayment said he expected others would do the same. "Everyone will," he said. "It makes no sense not to."

The looming debt repayment comes at a pivotal moment for the company — whose largest shareholder is President Trump — as it seeks to close a merger with lossmaking nuclear fusion start-up TAE Technologies by the end of the year. TMTG has already lent TAE $300mn.

Although TMTG's interim CEO Kevin McGurn has boasted of its "big balance sheet", many of the company's almost $2.5bn in assets may not be immediately available to generate cash to pay bondholders.

In its most recent quarterly filing, TMTG said it could enter a credit facility to refinance all or a portion of the convertible notes. But it also said such a move could be on unfavourable terms at a high interest rate and may not happen.
authors: George Steer and Antoine Gara and Ramsay Hodgson

articles.title: Hyperliquid's HYPE Token Shows Resilience as Crypto Market Crash Deepens
articles.summary: Hyperliquid's HYPE is outperforming Bitcoin and Ethereum amid the crypto crash. Bitunix analysts explain what's next.
articles.body:
Hyperliquid's HYPE token has lost roughly a quarter of its value since its peak. Yet amid the latest crypto market crash, it is holding up better than Bitcoin and Ethereum. Its derivatives market offers one possible explanation.

HYPE traded near $73 on Friday, down approximately 7% over seven days. Bitcoin lost more than 9% during the same period, while Ethereum dropped nearly 14%.

The token's recent decline followed a rally above $95 in late October, driven partly by excitement over a partnership involving Trade.xyz and Intercontinental Exchange, the New York Stock Exchange's parent company.

Why HYPE Is Holding Up Better Than Bitcoin and Ethereum

According to Bitunix's latest research, HYPE's notional open interest on Hyperliquid declined from $1.21 billion to $1.07 billion, approximately 12%.

Ethereum's open interest on the same platform fell more than 52% over a comparable period.

Open interest measures the value of outstanding futures positions. A smaller decline suggests traders have maintained more exposure to HYPE despite falling prices, although price changes also affect the dollar value of positions.

Bitunix also identified an early HYPE whale holding over $40 million in unrealized profits as of November 12.

Meanwhile, Hyperliquid Strategies reported holding 38.52 million HYPE, approximately 16% of circulating supply, as of September 30.

Why the Broader Crypto Market Keeps Falling

Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 on Friday, reaching approximately $68,700. Ethereum slipped toward $1,930.

Institutional withdrawals remain a concern. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded another $284.1 million in outflows on November 12, their sixth consecutive negative session.

Data shows approximately $2.8 billion in withdrawals since October 30.

Ethereum ETFs also lost $70.5 million on November 12.

Persistent US inflation has strengthened expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening. Falling prices have also triggered leveraged liquidations, accelerating the downturn.

WhaleRadar data showed $641 million in HYPE shorts against $515 million in longs among tracked large traders on November 13.

$70 remains the immediate level to watch.

Below that, the 200-day moving average near $68.60 offers another potential support area.

A deeper decline could threaten leveraged long positions clustered around $65.50.

A recovery above $74.40, followed by 76–77, would improve the short-term outlook.

HYPE's relative strength is encouraging, but sustained price recovery will depend on fresh buying demand and whether existing support levels survive the broader market downturn.
